the impact of BNP reduction on the prognostic implications associated with the occurrence of WRF in patients with AHF.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a BNP reduction >50% is associated with a lower risk of death and of WRF, while a BNP reduction ≤50% is associated only with a lower risk for death.

BNP reduction might be used as an indicator of successful deconvestion and may help in identifying patients with AHF who may benefit from aggressive decongestive therapy.

BNP reduction is a marker of successful decon-gestion and that WRF is a marker of unsuccessful decongestion.
